title.en: Word types I: the main words

summary.en: Wortarten: how to recognise German nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs and pronouns.
summary.bs: Wortarten: kako prepoznati njemačke imenice, glagole, pridjeve, priloge i zamjenice.

concepts.youtubeQuery: German parts of speech word types explained

en.one: Wortarten are word types: groups of words sorted by the job they do. German has about ten.
en.explain: The changeable ones (they take endings): Nomen (noun), Verb, Adjektiv, Artikel and Pronomen. The unchangeable ones: Adverb, Präposition, Konjunktion, Partikel and Interjektion. Numbers (Numerale) sit in between. Knowing the type tells you which rules apply: only verbs are conjugated, only nouns have a gender.
en.example: 'Der kleine Hund läuft schnell.' Der = article, kleine = adjective, Hund = noun, läuft = verb, schnell = adverb.
en.why: Almost every German grammar rule is about one word type, especially the changeable ones. Spotting the type is step one.
en.mixup: German writes every noun with a capital letter. That's a free clue English and Bosnian don't give you.

bs.one: Wortarten su vrste riječi: grupe riječi prema poslu koji rade. Njemački ih ima desetak.
bs.explain: Promjenjive (dobijaju nastavke): Nomen (imenica), Verb (glagol), Adjektiv (pridjev), Artikel (član) i Pronomen (zamjenica). Nepromjenjive: Adverb (prilog), Präposition (prijedlog), Konjunktion (veznik), Partikel (rječca) i Interjektion (uzvik). Brojevi (Numerale) su između. Kad znaš vrstu, znaš i pravila: samo se glagoli konjugiraju, samo imenice imaju rod.
bs.example: 'Der kleine Hund läuft schnell.' Der = član, kleine = pridjev, Hund = imenica, läuft = glagol, schnell = prilog.
bs.why: Gotovo svako njemačko gramatičko pravilo govori o jednoj vrsti riječi, posebno o promjenjivim. Prepoznavanje je prvi korak.
bs.mixup: Njemački piše svaku imenicu velikim slovom. To je besplatan znak koji ni bosanski ni engleski nemaju.

en.one: A Nomen (also called Substantiv) names a person, place, thing or idea: der Mann, die Stadt, das Buch, die Liebe.
en.explain: How to spot it: it always starts with a capital letter, it usually has an article in front (der, die, das, ein), and it has a gender, a number and a case. Words ending in -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -chen are always nouns.
en.example: 'Meine Schwester wohnt in Berlin und liebt Musik.' Nouns: Schwester, Berlin, Musik. All capitalised.
en.why: Nouns carry gender and case, and articles, adjectives and pronouns all have to agree with them.
en.mixup: Not every capitalised word is a noun: the first word of a sentence and the polite 'Sie' are capitalised too.

bs.one: Nomen (ili Substantiv) je imenica: osoba, mjesto, stvar ili ideja: der Mann, die Stadt, das Buch, die Liebe.
bs.explain: Kako je prepoznati: uvijek počinje velikim slovom, obično ima član ispred (der, die, das, ein), i ima rod, broj i padež. Riječi na -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -chen su uvijek imenice.
bs.example: 'Meine Schwester wohnt in Berlin und liebt Musik.' Imenice: Schwester, Berlin, Musik. Sve velikim slovom.
bs.why: Imenice nose rod i padež, a članovi, pridjevi i zamjenice se moraju slagati s njima.
bs.mixup: Nije svaka riječ s velikim slovom imenica: prva riječ rečenice i ljubazno 'Sie' se isto pišu velikim.

en.one: A Verb says what someone does or what state they are in: gehen, essen, denken, sein, haben.
en.explain: How to spot it: the dictionary form (Infinitiv) almost always ends in -en or -n (machen, wandern). In a sentence it changes its ending to match the subject (ich mache, du machst) and it has a fixed place: second in a statement.
en.example: 'Wir trinken Kaffee und sprechen über die Arbeit.' Verbs: trinken, sprechen.
en.why: The verb is the anchor of German word order. Find it first and the sentence becomes much easier to read.
en.mixup: German verbs can split in two: 'Ich rufe dich an' comes from 'anrufen'. The little 'an' at the end is part of the verb.

bs.one: Verb je glagol: kaže šta neko radi ili u kakvom je stanju: gehen, essen, denken, sein, haben.
bs.explain: Kako ga prepoznati: osnovni oblik (Infinitiv) skoro uvijek završava na -en ili -n (machen, wandern). U rečenici mijenja nastavak prema subjektu (ich mache, du machst) i ima stalno mjesto: drugo u izjavnoj rečenici.
bs.example: 'Wir trinken Kaffee und sprechen über die Arbeit.' Glagoli: trinken, sprechen.
bs.why: Glagol je sidro njemačkog reda riječi. Nađi ga prvo i rečenica postaje mnogo lakša.
bs.mixup: Njemački glagoli se mogu podijeliti: 'Ich rufe dich an' dolazi od 'anrufen'. Malo 'an' na kraju je dio glagola.

en.one: An Adjektiv describes a noun: what something is like. groß, rot, glücklich, teuer.
en.explain: How to spot it: it answers 'Wie?' (what kind?) and stands either before a noun (das große Haus) or after sein/werden (das Haus ist groß). Before a noun it takes an ending (-e, -en, -er, -es); after 'sein' it takes none. Typical endings: -ig, -lich, -isch, -bar, -los, -sam.
en.example: 'Der Kaffee ist heiß.' (no ending) vs. 'Ich trinke einen heißen Kaffee.' (ending -en)
en.why: Adjective endings are one of the trickiest parts of German. Recognising the adjective is the first step to getting them right.
en.mixup: In German most adjectives can also work as adverbs without any change: 'Er fährt schnell' (fast). English adds -ly, German doesn't.

bs.one: Adjektiv je pridjev: opisuje imenicu, kakvo je nešto. groß, rot, glücklich, teuer.
bs.explain: Kako ga prepoznati: odgovara na 'Wie?' (kakav?) i stoji ispred imenice (das große Haus) ili iza sein/werden (das Haus ist groß). Ispred imenice dobija nastavak (-e, -en, -er, -es), a iza 'sein' nema nastavka. Tipični završeci: -ig, -lich, -isch, -bar, -los, -sam.
bs.example: 'Der Kaffee ist heiß.' (bez nastavka) i 'Ich trinke einen heißen Kaffee.' (nastavak -en)
bs.why: Nastavci pridjeva su jedan od najtežih dijelova njemačkog. Prepoznati pridjev je prvi korak.
bs.mixup: U njemačkom se većina pridjeva može koristiti i kao prilog bez promjene: 'Er fährt schnell' (brzo).

en.one: An Adverb tells you how, when, where or how often something happens. It never changes its form.
en.explain: How to spot it: it answers Wann? (heute, morgen, jetzt), Wo? (hier, dort, oben), Wie? (gern, sehr, leider) or Wie oft? (oft, immer, nie). Unlike adjectives, adverbs never take endings.
en.example: 'Ich gehe heute gern ins Kino.' heute (when) and gern (how) are adverbs.
en.why: Adverbs often start a sentence ('Heute gehe ich…'), and then the verb still has to come second. That's where many mistakes happen.
en.mixup: 'Gern' has no English twin. 'Ich schwimme gern' = I like swimming. Add it to a verb to say you enjoy it.

bs.one: Adverb je prilog: kaže kako, kada, gdje ili koliko često se nešto dešava. Nikad ne mijenja oblik.
bs.explain: Kako ga prepoznati: odgovara na Wann? (heute, morgen, jetzt), Wo? (hier, dort, oben), Wie? (gern, sehr, leider) ili Wie oft? (oft, immer, nie). Za razliku od pridjeva, nikad nema nastavke.
bs.example: 'Ich gehe heute gern ins Kino.' heute (kada) i gern (kako) su prilozi.
bs.why: Prilozi često počinju rečenicu ('Heute gehe ich…'), a glagol i dalje mora biti drugi. Tu se često griješi.
bs.mixup: 'Gern' znači 'rado'. 'Ich schwimme gern' = rado plivam, volim plivati.

en.one: A Pronomen stands in for a noun: ich, du, er, sie, es, wir, ihr, sie, Sie.
en.explain: German pronouns follow the noun's grammatical gender, not its meaning: der Tisch → er, die Lampe → sie, das Auto → es. 'Sie' with a capital S is the polite 'you'. Pronouns also change with the case: ich, mich, mir.
en.example: 'Wo ist der Schlüssel? Er liegt auf dem Tisch.' The key is 'he' because it is 'der Schlüssel'.
en.why: Pronouns are short, but they are everywhere, and their case forms are your first practice with German cases.
en.mixup: Don't call every thing 'es'. A table is 'er' and a lamp is 'sie', because the pronoun copies the article.

bs.one: Pronomen je zamjenica: stoji umjesto imenice: ich, du, er, sie, es, wir, ihr, sie, Sie.
bs.explain: Njemačke zamjenice prate gramatički rod imenice: der Tisch → er, die Lampe → sie, das Auto → es. To je isto kao u bosanskom (stol/sto → on, lampa → ona). 'Sie' velikim slovom je ljubazno 'Vi'. Zamjenice se mijenjaju po padežima: ich, mich, mir.
bs.example: 'Wo ist der Schlüssel? Er liegt auf dem Tisch.' Ključ je 'er' jer je 'der Schlüssel'.
bs.why: Zamjenice su kratke, ali su svuda, i njihovi padežni oblici su tvoj prvi trening padeža.
bs.mixup: Rod se ne poklapa uvijek s bosanskim: 'das Mädchen' (djevojčica) je srednji rod, pa je zamjenica 'es'.

q.en: Which word is a noun in 'Wir kaufen heute Brot'?
q.bs: Koja riječ je imenica u 'Wir kaufen heute Brot'?

explain.en: Brot is capitalised and names a thing.
explain.bs: Brot je velikim slovom i imenuje stvar.

q.en: What does 'Er' refer to in 'Der Tisch ist neu. Er ist schön.'?
q.bs: Na šta se odnosi 'Er' u 'Der Tisch ist neu. Er ist schön.'?

explain.en: der Tisch → er. The pronoun copies the gender.
explain.bs: der Tisch → er. Zamjenica prati rod.

explain.en: 'morgen' (tomorrow) says when. 'Morgen' with a capital is the noun 'morning'.
explain.bs: 'morgen' (sutra) kaže kada. 'Morgen' velikim slovom je imenica 'jutro'.

q.en: Where does an adjective take no ending?

explain.en: After 'sein' an adjective has no ending.
